enonce_markdown: In a closed economy with no government the marginal propensity to consume is 0.75. Investment increases by 60 million FCFA. The resulting increase in equilibrium national income is:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

In a simple economy the multiplier is k = 1/(1 - MPC) = 1/MPS, and the change in income is ΔY = k × ΔInvestment.

### Solution

k = 1 / (1 - 0.75) = 1 / 0.25 = 4. ΔY = 4 × 60 = **240 million FCFA**. The value 45 multiplies by the MPC only, 80 divides by the MPC (1/0.75 is not the multiplier) and 180 uses MPC/MPS = 3 instead of 1/MPS. **Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: The accelerator principle states that the level of net investment depends mainly on:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Firms need a stock of capital proportional to the output they expect to sell, so investment responds to a change in output, not to its level.

### Solution

Net investment is the change in the capital stock needed to meet a change in demand: net investment = capital-output ratio × change in output. It therefore depends on the **rate of change of national income (output)**, so it can fall even while output is still rising, if output grows more slowly. The level of income, the interest rate and the MPC are not the basis of the accelerator. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the rate of change of national output

enonce_markdown: A clothing industry has a capital-output ratio of 3:1 (3 FCFA of capital for each 1 FCFA of annual output). Annual output rises from 400 million to 450 million FCFA, and capital worth 40 million FCFA wears out and must be replaced during the year. Gross investment in the year is:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Accelerator: net investment = capital-output ratio × change in output. Gross investment = net investment + replacement (depreciation).

### Solution

Net investment = 3 × (450 - 400) = 150 million FCFA. Gross investment = 150 + 40 = **190 million FCFA**. The value 50 is the change in output, 150 forgets replacement and 1,350 is the whole capital stock required (3 × 450). **Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown: A bakery chain has a capital-output ratio of 2:1 and existing capital of 2,000 million FCFA, exactly the amount needed to produce its annual sales of 1,000 million FCFA. Sales fall to 800 million FCFA. Capital worth 150 million FCFA wears out each year. Gross investment this year is:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the capital required for the new level of demand with the existing stock. If the stock is too large, firms do not replace worn-out capital; gross investment cannot be negative.

### Solution

Required capital = 2 × 800 = 1,600; existing capital = 2,000, so there is excess capacity of 400. Firms would like to reduce their capital by 400, but they can only do it by not replacing the 150 that wears out. Since 150 < 400, they do not replace anything: gross investment is **zero** (net investment is -150 and the excess capacity remains). Negative gross investment (-400 or -250) is not possible because installed machines cannot be turned back into money, and 150 would mean replacing capital that is not needed. **Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown:
In an open economy with a government, households spend 80% of any extra disposable income, income tax is a flat 25% of income, and 10% of any extra income is spent on imports.

(a) Identify the three leakages (withdrawals) in this economy. (3 marks)

(b) Calculate the value of the multiplier. (3 marks)

(c) Exports rise by 300 billion FCFA. Calculate the change in national income and compare the multiplier with the one obtained when there is only saving. (3 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The multiplier is the reciprocal of the marginal propensity to withdraw: k = 1/(1 - MPC(1 - t) + MPM), where t is the tax rate and MPM the marginal propensity to import.

### Solution

**(a)** The leakages are **saving**, **taxation** and **imports**.

**(b)** MPC after tax = 0.8 × (1 - 0.25) = 0.6. Marginal propensity to withdraw = 1 - 0.6 + 0.1 = 0.5 (saving 0.2 × 0.75 = 0.15, tax 0.25, imports 0.1: 0.15 + 0.25 + 0.1 = 0.5). k = 1 / 0.5 = **2**.

**(c)** ΔY = 2 × 300 = **600 billion FCFA**. With only saving (MPC = 0.8) the multiplier would be 1/(1 - 0.8) = 5, so taxes and imports cut it from 5 to 2: the more income leaks out of the circular flow, the smaller each round of spending and the smaller the multiplier.

enonce_markdown:
An economy has a capital-output ratio of 2:1 and depreciation is ignored. National income (billion FCFA) in five successive years is: Year 1: 1,000; Year 2: 1,000; Year 3: 1,100; Year 4: 1,200; Year 5: 1,200.

(a) Calculate net investment in Years 2 to 5. (4 marks)

(b) National income is the same in Years 4 and 5. Explain why net investment falls in Year 5. (2 marks)

(c) The multiplier is 2. Calculate the effect on national income of the change in investment between Year 4 and Year 5 and explain how the multiplier and accelerator can together make the economy turn from boom to slump. (4 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Accelerator: net investment = capital-output ratio × change in income. Multiplier: change in income = multiplier × change in investment. The two reinforce each other.

### Solution

**(a)** Net investment = 2 × change in income: Year 2: 2 × 0 = **0**; Year 3: 2 × 100 = **200**; Year 4: 2 × 100 = **200**; Year 5: 2 × 0 = **0**.

**(b)** Net investment depends on the **change** in income, not its level. In Year 5 income stops growing, so the existing capital stock is already sufficient and there is no need to add to it, even though income is at its highest level.

**(c)** Investment falls by 200, so by the multiplier national income falls by 2 × 200 = **400 billion FCFA** (in later years). This fall in income reduces the required capital stock; the accelerator then makes net investment negative or zero, which through the multiplier reduces income further. Slower growth at the top therefore starts a downward spiral: the two effects reinforce each other and can turn a boom into a recession. In practice the process is damped by government policy, by stocks of unused capacity and by the limits of full employment.
